title: Physics-Guided Discovery of Highly Nonlinear Parametric Partial Differential Equations

problem.claim: Discovering PDEs from scientific data is difficult when data are scarce and phenomena are complex.

gap.claim: Existing research has given limited attention to discovering PDEs with highly nonlinear coefficients from low-quality data.

contributions.claim: A physics-guided learning method for discovering PDEs with highly nonlinear coefficients from low-quality data.
The method encodes observation knowledge, including initial and boundary conditions, and incorporates basic physical principles and laws to guide model optimization.
The method discovers three-dimensional PDEs with highly nonlinear coefficients in the reported experiments.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors describe the method as novel and state that, for the first time, they are able to discover three-dimensional PDEs with highly nonlinear coefficients.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors theoretically show that their method strictly reduces coefficient estimation error relative to existing baselines and is robust against noise.
The authors report that extensive experiments show greater robustness to data noise and a large reduction in estimation error.
The authors report that all PDEs in the experiments were correctly discovered.

narrative_sequence.summary: PDEs fitted to scientific data can represent physical laws with explainable mechanisms.
Data-driven PDE discovery is limited by scarce data and complex phenomena, especially for highly nonlinear coefficients from low-quality data.
The proposed physics-guided learning method incorporates observation knowledge and physical principles into model optimization.

The authors report theoretical error reductions, noise robustness, lower experimental estimation error, correct discovery of the experimental PDEs, and discovery of three-dimensional PDEs with highly nonlinear coefficients.

source_observation.claim: The method incorporates initial and boundary conditions together with basic physical principles and laws during optimization.

interpretation.claim: Embedding available domain constraints may improve learning when observations are scarce or noisy.

application.claim: For scientific model discovery under limited or low-quality data, combine observational constraints with domain-law guidance during training.

exception.claim: The abstract does not specify which types of PDEs, noise levels, data regimes, or domains may limit this lesson.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the model architecture, optimization procedure, or baseline implementations.
The abstract does not provide datasets, quantitative error values, noise levels, or experimental settings.
The abstract does not describe the theoretical assumptions or proof details behind the error guarantee.
